official.description_text:
Doctoral student in probabilistic machine learning for fluid mechanics
Apply for position
KTH Royal Institute of Technology, School of Engineering Sciences
Project description
Third-cycle subject:
Engineering Mechanics
FLOW
is a strong community of researchers engaged in fundamental and applied research in fluid mechanics within the department of Engineering Mechanics.
We are currently seeking a PhD student in probabilistic machine learning to join the Fluids and Surfaces Group within FLOW. AI is becoming a critical investment across science and engineering, but fluid mechanics poses particular challenges: flows are often high-dimensional and chaotic, and couple physical processes across many scales.
This position offers an exciting opportunity for a highly motivated candidate to develop trustworthy probabilistic methods for inference, optimization and data assimilation. These methods will integrate simulations and experimental data into reliable tools for the design, prediction and control of complex fluid systems.
The work focuses on turbulent flows that carry electric charge, as found for example in power transformers. These systems involve coupled processes that are only partly understood, and measurements are sparse and costly. This makes them an ideal testbed, where models must be calibrated, uncertainties quantified and experiments chosen with care, with direct impact on safer and more sustainable power infrastructure. The project is funded by
Digital Futures
och
Hitachi Energy
Supervision:
Shervin Bagheri
and Ozan Öktem are proposed to supervise the student. Decisions are made on admission.
Admission requirements
To be admitted to postgraduate education (Chapter 7, 39 § Swedish Higher Education Ordinance), the applicant must have basic eligibility in accordance with either of the following:
passed a second cycle degree (for example a master's degree), or
completed course requirements of at least 240 higher education credits, of which at least 60 second-cycle higher education credits, or
acquired, in some other way within or outside the country, substantially equivalent knowledge
In addition to the above, there is also a
mandatory requirement for English equivalent to English B/6.
Selection
In order to succeed as a doctoral student at KTH you need to be goal oriented and persevering in your work. During the selection process, candidates will be assessed upon their ability to:
independently pursue his or her work
collaborate with others,
have a professional approach and
analyze and work with complex issues.
It is meritorious to have experience with fluid mechanics, machine learning and scientific computing, in particular, turbulent flows, Bayesian inference, probabilistic methods and generative AI
After the qualification requirements, great emphasis will be placed on personal skills.
Target degree: Doctoral degree
Information regarding admission and employment
Only those admitted to postgraduate education may be employed as a doctoral student. The total length of employment may not be longer than what corresponds to full-time doctoral education in four years' time. An employed doctoral student can, to a limited extent (maximum 20%), perform certain tasks within their role, e.g. training and administration. A new position as a doctoral student is for a maximum of one year, and then the employment may be renewed for a maximum of two years at a time. In the case of studies that are to be completed with a licentiate degree, the total period of employment may not be longer than what corresponds to full-time doctoral education for two years.
As a doctoral student, you are entitled to a workplace with
many employee benefits
and monthly salary according to
KTH’s Doctoral student salary agreement

To apply for the position
Apply for the position and admission through KTH's recruitment system. It is the applicant’s responsibility to ensure that the application is complete in accordance with the instructions in the advertisement.
Applications must include the following elements:
Copies of diplomas and grades from previous university studies and certificates of fulfilled
language requirements (see above)
. Translations into English or Swedish if the original document is not issued in one of these languages. Copies of originals must be
certified
.
CV including your relevant professional experience and knowledge.
Application letter with a brief description of why you want to pursue research studies, about what your academic interests are and how they relate to your previous studies and future goals. (Maximum 2 pages long)

Applications must be received at the last closing date at midnight, CET/CEST (Central European Time/Central European Summer Time).

ai.summary: A 3–4 year PhD position at KTH (Stockholm) in probabilistic machine learning applied to fluid mechanics, specifically electric-charge-carrying turbulent flows in power transformers. The research integrates simulations, experimental data, and machine learning for inference, optimization, and control. Funded by Digital Futures and Hitachi Energy.

thematic_fit.rationale: The posting is centred on computational fluid mechanics, probabilistic inference, and power systems engineering. The researcher's thematic focus is human-centred XR, collaborative immersive learning, and spatial cognition. These domains do not intersect.

methodological_fit.rationale: The position requires probabilistic methods, Bayesian inference, generative AI, and scientific computing. The researcher has no documented experience in machine learning, Bayesian statistics, or computational physics. While both contexts involve validation (simulations + experiments vs. user studies + spatial measures), the technical methodologies are entirely distinct. The posting explicitly warns against pure ML algorithm development as poor fit for human-centred research; this is precisely that.

growth_value.rationale: This position would develop advanced machine learning, probabilistic modelling, and computational physics expertise. These skills do not advance human-centred XR research. They would consume 3–4 years without building capabilities in user-centred design, immersive systems, spatial cognition assessment, or HCI evaluation.

strategic_value.rationale: KTH is reputable; Stockholm is in a target geography. However, the supervising group (FLOW, Bagheri, Öktem) specializes in fluid mechanics and computational methods—not HCI, XR, or user-centred research. The industrial partner (Hitachi Energy) is not in immersive technology or learning systems. The network and funding are solid, but misaligned with career goals.

eligibility_flags: Posting values 'experience with fluid mechanics, machine learning and scientific computing'—researcher has none of these. Python is listed in taxonomy but researcher rates self as 'beginner'.
Master's degree requirement is general; researcher's MMU MSc by Research should be eligible on degree level, but disciplinary alignment weak.
risks: Core exclusion criterion applies: this is pure machine-learning algorithm development for physics simulation—explicitly flagged as poor fit for human-centred researchers.
Skill gap too large: transition from XR design/evaluation to advanced probabilistic ML is steep and would require intensive foundational retraining.
Network isolation: FLOW group and collaborators are computational scientists, not HCI/XR/social systems researchers.

eligibility_reasons: funding/salary not confirmed on the posting
